title: Protocol for SARS-CoV-2 infection of kidney organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells
protocol: Grow Vero-E6 Cells until 90% confluency in two 75-cm² flasks.
Plate Vero-E6 Cells at 6.5–9.5 × 10⁴ cells/cm² in ten 75-cm² flasks in Complete Growth Medium.
Incubate the flasks at 37°C and 5% CO₂.
Count the cells the day after seeding.
Calculate the volume of virus inoculum to achieve an MOI of 0.01 PFU per cell using the provided formula.
Thaw a vial of SARS-CoV-2 seed stock at 20°C–22°C.
Dilute the necessary volume of virus in DMEM supplemented with 2% FBS.
Remove the medium from 90% confluent Vero-E6 Cell monolayers.
Wash once with 3 mL of PBS per flask.
Add 3 mL of Complete Infection Medium containing the virus to each 75-cm2 flask.
For mock-infected control, add 3 mL of fresh Complete Infection Medium to a flask.
Incubate flasks at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Add 7 mL of Complete Growth Medium to each flask after 1 hour.
Monitor flasks daily for 48-72 hours for cytopathic effect (CPE) using an inverted microscope.
Compare infected flasks with mock-infected flask as a negative control.
Harvest the virus supernatant from infected Vero-E6 Cell monolayers when 90% CPE is observed.
Collect the virus supernatant into sterile 15 mL conical tubes.
Discard mock-infected controls.
Dispose flasks, remaining cells and pipettes as infectious waste.
Centrifuge the tubes at 450 × g for 5 min at 4°C to pellet cell debris.
Prepare 200–500 μL aliquots of supernatant in labeled 2 mL screw-tubes.
Store virus stock aliquots immediately at -80°C.
Plate 8 × 10^5 Vero-E6 cells in 3 mL of complete growth medium per well of a 6-well plate.
Incubate the plate for 12–16 hours at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Check under the microscope that cells formed a confluent compact monolayer in each well.
Heat the 1% agarose solution in a microwave.
Keep the bottle of heated 1% agarose solution in a water bath at 55°C.
Prepare EMEM/14% FBS medium and equilibrate it at 20°C–22°C.
Dilute the virus stock as indicated for titration.
Label seven Eppendorf tubes with each dilution (10^-1, 10^-2, 10^-3, 10^-4, 10^-5, 10^-6, 10^-7).
Add 900 μL of complete infection medium to each tube.
Add 100 μL of the virus sample to be titrated to the first tube (10^-1) to make the first dilution.
Mix by vortexing the tube containing the first dilution.
Take 100 μL of the first virus dilution and transfer it to the second tube (10^-2).
Mix by vortexing the tube containing the second dilution.
Repeat steps v-vi by taking 100 μL of the newly created virus dilution and adding it to the next Eppendorf tube until a 10-7 dilution is reached.
Discard tips directly without pipetting between each dilution.
Infect Vero-E6 Cell monolayers prepared in step 7 with serial virus dilutions.
Label each well of a 6-well plate with corresponding dilutions ranging from 10-3 to 10-7 and one well for non-infected control.
Remove existing Complete Growth Medium from the Vero-E6 Cell monolayers.
Wash once with 1 mL of PBS 1× per well.
Transfer 500 μL of the 10-7 virus dilution to one well of the labelled 6-well plate.
Repeat this step for 10-6 to 10-3 dilutions, starting from the most diluted sample.
Incubate plates at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 1 h to allow virus attachment.
Redistribute supernatant by rocking plates carefully every 15 min during incubation.
Calculate volume of Plaque Assay Overlay Medium needed, counting 3 mL per well of 6-well plate plus 3 mL extra as a control.
Remove viral inoculums from each well after 1 h and close the plate.
Change tips between each well.
Prepare Plaque Assay Overlay Medium by mixing 1 volume of 1% Agarose solution with 1 volume of EMEM/14% FBS Medium in a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 3 mL of Plaque Assay Overlay Medium to each well of the 6-well plate.
Incubate the plates at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 3 days to allow plaque formation.
Visualize plaques by Crystal Violet staining 3 days post-infection.
Add 1 mL of 25% Formaldehyde solution per well on top of the agarose layer.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Carefully remove the agarose layer using a flat spatula.
Dispose of the removed agarose layer as infectious waste.
Do not touch the cell monolayer with the spatula to avoid scratching the monolayer.
Add 1 mL of 1% Crystal Violet staining solution per well of the 6-well plate.
Incubate for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Remove the Crystal Violet solution from the wells.
Wash the wells three times with 3 mL of tap water per well.
Properly discard formaldehyde and crystal violet solutions as toxic waste according to institutional rules.
Leave the plate inverted to air-dry the stained monolayers.
Count the plaques in each well at each virus dilution.
Discount wells with fewer than 5 or greater than 100 plaques.
Note plaque size and morphology.
Use the negative control, which should present a uniform, purple-stained monolayer, as a reference control.
Identify the first dilution in which a maximum of 50 plaques can be counted.
Determine the viral titer using the formula: Plaque forming units (PFU)/mL = [average number of plaques] / [dilution factor × volume of inoculum added in mL].
Plate 30,000 Vero-E6 Cells in 100 μL of Complete Growth Medium per well of a 96-BCB plate.
Incubate the plate 12–16 h at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Remove the 100 μL of media from the first row of wells of the 96-BCB plate containing Vero-E6 Cells.
Add 110 μL of non-diluted virus stock per well.
Use a multichannel pipette to remove 10 μL of virus from the first row of wells and place it in the second row of wells.
Gently pipette up and down to mix the virus with the media.
Remove 10 μL of the virus dilution from the second row of wells and add it to the third row for a 10-2 dilution.
Repeat by removing 10 μL of each new dilution and adding it to the next well until reaching a 10-6 dilution.
Incubate the 96-BCB plate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Change pipette tips for each dilution step.
Mix contents thoroughly before making subsequent dilutions.
Leave one lane as a mock sample without virus addition.
Remove virus-infected media after incubation.
Wash wells once with 200 μL of PBS per well.
Add 200 μL of 4% Paraformaldehyde to each well and incubate at 20°C–22°C for 20 minutes.
Submerge the full plate in 4% PFA solution for an additional 20 minutes after initial fixation.
Wash wells three times with 200 μL of PBS per well post-fixation.
Add 100 μL of PBS supplemented with 0.05% Triton-X to each well.
Incubate at 20°C–22°C for 15 minutes prior to immunolabelling.
Remove the solution from the wells.
Add 100 μL per well of the Intercept® (PBS) Blocking Buffer.
Incubate at 20°C–22°C for 30 min.
Remove the Intercept® (PBS) Blocking Buffer from the wells.
Add 100 μL of the primary antibody solution to each well.
Incubate at 20°C–22°C for 1 h.
Remove the primary antibody solution from the wells.
Wash 3 times with 100 μL of PBS 1× per well.

Prepare the necessary secondary antibody solution by diluting the anti-mouse IR800CW secondary antibody at 1:5000 dilution ratio in Intercept® (PBS) Blocking Buffer and supplementing it with nuclear dye Draq5 at 1:10000 dilution ratio.
Add 100 μL of the secondary antibody solution supplemented with the nuclear dye Draq5 to each well.
Incubate at 20°C–22°C in the dark for 45 min.
Remove the secondary antibody solution from the wells.
Wash the wells 3 times with 100 μL of PBS 1× per well.
Add 200 μL of PBS 1× to each well.
Image the plate in an Odyssey® Imaging System (Odyssey® M, CLx or DLx models by Licor).
Analyse with the Empiria Studio® Software.
Use PBS 1× supplemented with 5% BSA as blocking buffer.
Incubate the sample with a secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 at a 1:1000 dilution ratio in blocking buffer.
Incubate the sample with nuclear stain DAPI at a 1:2000 dilution ratio in blocking buffer.
Determine the average intensity of mock-infected cells.
Calculate the standard deviation of the intensity of mock-infected cells.
Multiply the standard deviation by 2.
Add twice the standard deviation to the average mock value.
Consider all values above this calculated threshold as positive wells.
Use the Spearman-Karber method to calculate the TCID50/mL.
Log10 of the reciprocal of the highest dilution at which all wells are positive equals x0.
Determine the log10 of the dilution factor, d.
Count the number of wells used in each individual dilution as ni.
Record the number of positive wells out of ni as ri.
Prepare one 24-well plate with VTN-N coating using 0.3 mL of VTN-N solution per well.
Disaggregate 3 wells of a 6-well plate containing hPSCs at 80% confluency into small cell clusters.
Collect the resultant cell clusters in 6 mL of Complete E8 Medium in a sterile 15 mL conical tube.
Count cells using a Countess Automated Cell Counter.
Plate between 1–2 × 105 viable cells per well of VTN-N coated 24-well plate.
Calculate the volume of Complete E8 medium needed to achieve a cell density between 2–4 × 105 cells/mL.
Re-suspend the cells and plate 0.5 mL of the cell suspension per well of VTN-N coated 24-well plate.
Refresh with Complete E8 Medium after 24 hours.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Gently aspirate the Complete E8 medium from each well without disrupting the hPSC colonies on day 0.
Add 0.5 mL of Complete Advanced RPMI 1640 Basal Medium supplemented with 8 μM CHIR to each well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Replace the media with fresh Posterior Primitive Streak Induction Medium every 24 hours for 3 consecutive days.
Gently aspirate Posterior Primitive Streak Induction Medium from each well of the 24-well plate.
Add 0.5 mL of Intermediate Mesoderm Induction Medium supplemented with FGF9, Heparin, and Activin A to each well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
On day 4, observe cells under a microscope and check for a tight homogeneous cell monolayer.
Gently aspirate Intermediate Mesoderm Induction Medium from each well of the 24-well plate.
Add 0.5 mL of CHIR-Pulse Organoid Induction Medium supplemented with CHIR, FGF9, and Heparin to each well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
After 1 hour, dissociate cell monolayers to generate a single cell suspension.
Gently aspirate the supernatant without mechanically disrupting the cell monolayer during media changes and washing steps.
Rinse cell monolayers by adding 0.5 mL of PBS 1× per well of 24-well plate.
Add 300 μL of TrypLE™ Express and incubate at 20°C–22°C for 1 min.
Gently aspirate the TrypLE™ Express without mechanically disrupting the cell monolayer.
Dissociate the cell monolayers by flushing 0.5 mL of Complete Advanced RPMI 1640 Basal Medium supplemented with FGF9 and heparin to each well of 24-well plate.
Collect the resultant cell suspension in a 50 mL conical tube.
Mix 10 μL of cell suspension with 10 μL of 0.4% Trypan Blue Stain, mix thoroughly, and pipette 10 μL into a CountessTM cell counting chamber slide.
Count viable cells using a Countess Automated Cell Counter or Neubauer chamber.
Plate 1 × 10^5 cells per well of Nunc™ 96-Well Polystyrene Conical Bottom (V-bottom) MicroWell™ plate.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min and re-suspend the cells in Kidney Organoid Differentiation Medium at a density of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Use a 12-multichannel pipette to plate 100 μL of the resultant cell suspension per well of V-bottom MicroWell™ plate.
Centrifuge V-bottom MicroWell™ plates at 300 × g for 3 min to induce the formation of intermediate mesoderm-committed spheroids.
Incubate the resultant organoids at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Culture the organoids for 7 additional days (day 4 to day 11) in Kidney Organoid Differentiation Medium.
Change medium every second day.
Use a 12-multichannel pipette to remove the media avoiding touching the organoids.
Add 100 μL of fresh Kidney Organoid Differentiation Medium per well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
On day 11 of differentiation, remove growth factors by culturing organoids in 100 μL per well of Complete Advanced RPMI 1640 Medium.
Culture developing kidney organoids for 5 additional days (day 11 to day 16) in Complete Advanced RPMI 1640 Medium.
Change medium every second day.
Maintain kidney organoids in V-bottom MicroWell™ plate.
Expose control organoids to Normoglycemic Medium only for 7 days (from day 16 to day 23).
Expose diabetic organoids alternately to Normoglycemic and Hyperglycemic Media every day for 7 days (from day 16 to day 23).
Replace media with 100 μl of Normoglycemic or Hyperglycemic Medium per well daily using a 12-multichannel pipette.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Ensure complete replacement of medium from each well for proper exposure of kidney organoids to desired glucose concentration.
Avoid aspirating kidney organoids during medium changes.
Infect control and diabetic kidney organoids with SARS-CoV-2 after 7 days of treatment.
Calculate the amount of virus stock needed to infect organoids with 106 PFU per organoid.
Prepare 24 organoids for each condition, using 12 for qRT-PCR analysis and 12 for immunofluorescence.
Keep some organoids as mock controls.
Infect kidney organoids with 106 PFU of SARS-CoV-2 per organoid.
Place one organoid per well in a Low-Attachment Surface 96-well plate using wide orifice pipette tips.
Add 100 μL of Normoglycemic or Hyperglycemic Medium to each well containing an organoid.
Use pipette tips with wide openings to collect or handle organoids.
Keep mock and SARS-CoV-2 infected kidney organoids in separate plates to avoid cross-contamination.
Dilute the virus stock into Complete Infection Medium (Virus Working Solution) at a concentration of 10^6 PFU per 100 μL.
Remove media from each well containing organoids.
Add 100 μL of Virus Working Solution per well for infected samples.
Add an equal volume of medium without virus to mock controls.
Incubate the mock or infected organoids at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
After 1 hour, remove the supernatant from each well and dispose as infectious waste.
Wash organoids three times with 100 μL of Normoglycemic or Hyperglycemic Medium per well to remove unbound virus.
Dispose of the washing medium as infectious waste.
Add 100 μL of fresh Normoglycemic or Hyperglycemic Medium per well and incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 1 day.
Collect 24 organoids per condition using a wide-opening pipette tip into two Eppendorf tubes (12 organoids per tube).
Wash the collected organoids three times with 500 μL of PBS 1× per tube to remove unbound virus.
Remove the supernatant and dispose as infectious waste.
Add 500 μL of Trizol to 12 organoids for viral RNA detection by qRT-PCR.
Store the Trizol-treated samples at −80°C for further analysis.
For NP detection by immunofluorescence, add 500 μL of 4% PFA per Eppendorf tube.
Incubate the samples with 4% PFA in a fume hood for 12–16 hours at 4°C.
Remove the fixative from the samples in a fume hood.
Wash the fixed organoids three times with 500 μL of PBS.
Store the fixed samples in PBS at 4°C for further analysis.
Divide fixed organoid specimens for either whole mount immunofluorescence or immunofluorescence in paraffin sections.
Place 3 organoids per experimental condition in each well of a 24-well plate with 400 μL of Tris-Buffered Saline (TBS) 1×.
Place 1 additional organoid per experimental condition in individual wells of a 24-well plate with 400 μL of 1× TBS for secondary antibody controls.
Shake the plate in an orbital shaker at 20°C–22°C for 10 min.
Remove the TBS 1× from each well of the 24-well plate.
Add 400 μL of TBS 1× supplemented with 1% Triton X-100 and 6% Donkey Serum (6%DS-Blocking Buffer) per well.
Incubate for 4 h at 20°C–22°C in an orbital shaker.
Remove the 6%DS-Blocking Buffer from each well of the 24-well plate.
Wash once with 400 μL of TBS 1× per well for 15 min at 20°C–22°C in an orbital shaker.
Remove the TBS 1× and add 6–8 drops of the Streptavidin Solution to each well to cover the organoids.
Incubate for 20 min at 20°C–22°C under constant shaking.
Wash the organoids once with 400 μL of TBS 1× per well for 15 min at 20°C–22°C in an orbital shaker.
Remove the TBS 1× from each well and add 6–8 drops of the Biotin Solution to each well to cover the organoids.
Incubate for 20 min at 20°C–22°C under constant shaking.
Wash the organoids once with 400 μL of TBS 1× per well for 15 min at 20°C–22°C in an orbital shaker.
Remove the TBS 1× from each well and add 400 μL of TBS 1× supplemented with 1% Triton X-100 and 1% Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA).
Pause point: Organoids can be stored in BSA-1%T-Blocking Buffer for 12–16 h at 4°C.
Prepare the necessary primary antibody solution by diluting the correspondent primary antibodies in BSA-1%T-Blocking Buffer.
Remove the BSA-1%T-Blocking Buffer from each well and cover the organoids with 250 μL of the primary antibody solution.
Incubate for 1 h at 20°C–22°C under constant shaking, then 12–16 h at 4°C and finally at 20°C–22°C for an additional 1 h, under shaking conditions.
Wash organoids 3 times with 400 μL of BSA-1%T-Blocking Buffer per well for 20 min at 20°C–22°C under shaking conditions.
Prepare the necessary secondary antibody solution by diluting the correspondent secondary antibodies in BSA-1%T-Blocking Buffer.
Centrifuge the secondary antibody solution at 1,200 × g.
Take the supernatant and discard any pellet of precipitates that might have been formed.
Remove the BSA-1%T-Blocking Buffer from each well.
Cover the organoids with 250 μL of the secondary antibody solution per well.
Incubate for 4 h at 20°C–22°C in an orbital shaker in darkness.
Wash the organoids 3 times with 400 μL of TBS 1× per well for 20 min at 20°C–22°C under shaking conditions.
Remove the TBS 1× from each well.
Cover the organoids with 250 μL of the DAPI working solution (dilute the DAPI stock at 1:5000 ratio in TBS 1×).
Incubate for 12–16 h at 4°C.
Remove DAPI solution from each well.
Add 400 μL of PBS 1× to each well.
Keep immunolabelled organoids at 4°C in the darkness until mounting for imaging.
Transfer one immunolabelled organoid onto a rectangular cover slip using a pipette tip, minimizing the amount of PBS 1× collected.
Remove as much residual PBS 1× solution as possible from the cover slip.
Add a drop of 100 μL RapiClear® 1.47 clearing reagent to completely immerse the organoid in the clearing solution.
Incubate for 20 minutes at 20°C–22°C until the organoid becomes transparent.
Place another rectangular cover slip on top of the cleared organoid, ensuring the clearing solution covers the entire surface.
Store mounted organoid samples at 4°C in the darkness until imaging.
Heat the 0.8% low melting agarose solution at 60°C until liquid.
Maintain the agarose solution warm at 37°C.
Place a layer of 100 μL of 0.8% low melting agarose solution into the bottom of a plastic cryomold.
Allow to cool down for 5 minutes.
Re-suspend fixed kidney organoids samples in 150 μL of warm 0.8% low melting agarose (37°C) and transfer to the cryomold.
Place at least three fixed kidney organoid specimens per cryomold.
Ensure that organoids are surrounded by agarose without introducing air bubbles.
Place the prepared molds on ice until the agarose is solidified.
Transfer the agarose blocks containing the organoids from the mold into a 12-well plate with cold PBS 1×.
Store the agarose blocks at 4°C, up to one week, for further paraffin embedding in PBS 1× supplemented with 0.02% Sodium Azide.
Transfer the agarose blocks prepared in step 33a into embedding cassettes using a spatula.
Proceed to standard dehydration in an automatic tissue processor.
Embed the dehydrated tissues in paraffin at 58°C using metallic molds.
Obtain paraffin blocks and store them at 20°C–22°C.
Cool down the paraffin blocks on a cold plate.
Prepare organoid sections of 3 μm-thickness using a rotary microtome.
Guide the ribbon of paraffin sections into the water bath at 40°C to unfold sections.
Collect the paraffin sections onto charged glass slides.
Prepare 20 slides with 2 sections per slide.
Properly label each slide.
Dry the slides in an oven at 60°C for 12–16 hours.
Store the dried slides at 20°C–22°C for up to 6-12 months.
Select the appropriate slides for immunofluorescence analysis.
Perform Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) staining on slides number 5, 10, and 15.
Observe H&E-stained slides under the microscope to identify slides containing organoid sections.
Select at least 2 slides per sample for immunofluorescence analysis of a given combination of primary antibodies.
Take an additional slide for performing the secondary antibody control.
Deparaffinize and re-hydrate the selected slides.
Immerse the slides in citrate buffer (pH 6).
Autoclave the immersed slides at 95°C for 20 min.
Cool down the slides to 20°C–22°C.
Wash the slides with 0.5–1 mL TBS 1× per slide.
Cover the organoid sections in each slide with 0.5–1 mL of TBS 1× containing 1% Triton X-100 and 3% Donkey Serum (3%DS-Blocking Buffer).
Incubate the samples for 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Perform an additional blocking step with the Streptavidin/Biotin Blocking Kit as detailed in step 32d.
Cover the organoid sections in each slide with 0.5-1 mL of TBS 1× containing 0.5% Triton X-100 and 1% BSA (BSA-0.5%T-Blocking Buffer).
Prepare the necessary primary antibody solution by diluting the corresponding primary antibodies in BSA-0.5%T-Blocking Buffer.
Remove the BSA-0.5%T-Blocking Buffer from the slides.
Draw a circle around organoid sections in each slide using a hydrophobic barrier pen.
Cover organoid sections in each slide with 200 μL of the primary antibody solution.
Incubate the slides for 12–16 h at 4°C.
Wash the slides 3 times with 0.5-1 mL of BSA-0.5%T-Blocking Buffer per slide for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Dilute corresponding secondary antibodies in BSA-0.5%T-Blocking Buffer.
Cover organoid sections on each slide with 200 μL of the secondary antibody solution.
Incubate slides for 2 hours at 20°C–22°C in darkness.
Wash slides three times with 0.5–1 mL of TBS 1× per slide for 5 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Counterstain nuclei with DAPI for 30 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Remove DAPI solution from the slides.
Deposit 3–4 drops of Fluoromount-G mounting medium on top of each slide.
Place a rectangular coverslip on top of the slide carefully.
Carefully remove excess mounting media using absorbent paper.
Seal borders of the slide with nail polish.
Acquire images on a confocal microscope.
Use Fiji ImageJ2 version 2.3.0 software for image processing and generation of TIFF files.
Set scan mode to frame.
Set frame size to 1024 × 1024.
Set line average to 2.
Enable bidirectional scanning.
Set speed to 7.
Use a 10× dry objective (Plan-Apochromat 10×/0.3 M27) or a 25× multi-immersion objective (Plan-Apochromat 25×/0.8 Imm Corr DIC M27).
Activate tile scan mode to indicate the borders of the organoid in x/y direction.
Activate z-stack mode to define upper and lower limits of the sample in the z direction.
Use a 40× oil immersion objective (Plan-Apochromat 40×/1.3 Oil DIC M27) for high magnification details of the sample.
